about: The DSP under peak finding and the live spectrum. The union of the three editions' cases; the expected values are Swift's (its production code, run by a minting test), in 32-bit Float — numbers are compared at 'tolerance': |actual - expected| <= relative * |expected| + absolute; NaN and the infinities are strings. 'spectra': named magnitude/frequency arrays the cases use. 'parabolicInterpolate': a spectrum (inline or named) and a peak index → the interpolated frequency and magnitude (TapToneAnalyzer.parabolicInterpolate). 'calculateQFactor': a named spectrum, a peak index and its magnitude → Q and the -3 dB bandwidth (TapToneAnalyzer.calculateQFactor). 'signals': a signal (silence; a constant: 'value' plus an alternating ±'alternating', i.e. DC and Nyquist; or a tone: count, amplitude, frequency, sample rate; 'fftSize' is the analyzer's FFT size) through one RealtimeFFTAnalyzer path — gatedFFT (computeGatedFFT: every bin -inf, or the loudest bin and its frequency; binCount), computeFFT (the live FFT: binCount; every bin -inf, the loudest bin at index × rate / fftSize, or bin 0 and the last bin), performFFT (the live peak, peakFrequency / peakMagnitude, on a fresh analyzer at 48 kHz), processRawSamples (one chunk: inputLevelDB, what detection sees, and readoutLevelDB).
